entities.summary:
The Wheel of Time is a landmark series of epic fantasy novels authored primarily by Robert Jordan, with the final volumes completed by Brandon Sanderson after Jordan's death in 2007. Spanning 14 books published from 1990 to 2013, this intricate narrative is set in a richly developed world where magic, political intrigue, and mythological elements converge. Its global significance lies in its profound influence on the genre of fantasy literature, establishing a template for complex world-building, deep character arcs, and overarching plots that have inspired countless authors and adaptations across various media.

Central to The Wheel of Time's narrative is the battle between the Dragon Reborn, Rand al'Thor, and the Dark One, a malevolent force threatening to unravel reality. The series intricately weaves together diverse cultures, philosophies, and historical themes, reflecting a keen understanding of human nature and societal dynamics. The first book, "The Eye of the World," was released in January 1990, introducing readers to a richly detailed universe that includes the Aes Sedai, a powerful organization of female magic users, and the intricate relationships among various nations and peoples.

The legacy of The Wheel of Time extends beyond its pages, as it has spawned a dedicated fan base, critical scholarly analyses, and adaptations into television and graphic novels, most notably the Amazon Prime series launched in 2021. Its impact on the fantasy genre is visible in the works of subsequent authors who have drawn inspiration from Jordan's complex narrative structure and character development. Furthermore, the series has prompted discussions on themes of power, gender, and morality in fantastical settings, influencing both reader and writer perspectives in contemporary literature.
